confidence_note: The refrigerator and thermostat examples are described in a detailed secondary article about Norman's conceptual models; the book text itself was not read, so salad and ice-cream details and the day-long settling time are as that article reports them. The old trash-can example was not found for this book and was dropped.
facts: A conceptual model is usually highly simplified and need not be complete or accurate as long as it is useful.
Refrigerator: two controls labelled freezer and fresh food suggest each sets its own compartment.

In fact one sets the compressor level and the other shifts how cold air is split; a colder freezer also chills the fresh-food section (salad can freeze) and a colder fresh-food section takes cold from the freezer (ice cream can thaw).
Temperatures take about a day to settle, so adjusting takes about a week; Norman says the controls suggest a false conceptual model.
Thermostat: people believe turning the dial to the top warms a cold room faster; the setting only decides when heating shuts off, heat output is the same.
A critic argues the fridge's real flaw is the controls themselves, not the labels.
scene_details: A dial turned to the top.
A salad frozen solid, ice cream thawing.
A day for the temperature to settle.
tension: People operate a device with a picture that does not match how it works.
opening_idea: Start with the thermostat turned to the top.

lessons.idea: Ask people what they think a control does, and fix the setup where they are wrong.

reflect_final: What picture do the people who use your system hold of how it works, and where does that differ from what really happens?

use_cases.situation: Training staff on a new tool
use_cases.move: Norman's fridge controls suggested a false model; I'll ask what each of you thinks this button does before I explain it.
Check what each person believes the dial does, then turn it once and watch.

use_cases.situation: Fiddling with a device that never behaves
use_cases.move: Ask what picture of it you are working from and test it.

pocket_idea: Turn the dial to the top and the room warms no faster, because the dial only says when to stop.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Turning a thermostat to the top does not warm the room faster.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Thermostat, fridge, false model, a week to adjust.
